_comment: klt erc supply spec for sg13cmos5l-bandgap_top.gds -- the structural
power-delivery artifact T1 item 11 (klayout-tools#2025) requires, per
issue #225. Tie declaration added by issue #233 (see the ties[] block
comment below).
Run it against the committed top-level assembly GDS:
klt erc layout/sg13cmos5l-bandgap_top/sg13cmos5l-bandgap_top.gds \
layout/sg13cmos5l-bandgap_top/erc-supply-spec.json --format json
The stream has exactly one top cell (sg13cmos5l_bandgap_top), so --top is
not needed. Commit the JSON output as erc_report.json next to this spec.
What this spec asserts, and why each field is shaped this way:
- stackup[0] MUST carry role: "gate" (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at GatPoly (5/0), CMOS5L's gate-poly conductor. Every
layer/datatype below is read from the resolved CMOS5L technology's own
libs.tech/klayout/tech/sg13cmos5l.lyp <name>/<source> entries (IHP
release v0.2.0) and cross-checked against klt's curated sg13cmos5l deck
(layout/common_sg13cmos5l.py's layer table records the same read-off;
layout/README.md 'SG13CMOS5L layer numbers' documents it) -- not copied
from gf180mcu's or sky130's spec.
- active_layer (Activ, 1/0) makes the antenna denominator poly ∩ diff
instead of raw poly area. This block carries real poly resistors
(R1/R2 rppd, RPU rhigh) whose GatPoly bars have no gate oxide; without
active_layer they would enter gates[] as pseudo-gates and report
non-physical antenna ratios (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md, 'Gate
area: poly ∩ diff vs. raw poly area').
- Metal1 (8/0) is the only routing metal this single-metal block uses
(buses and approach stubs are Metal1; inter-cell risers are GatPoly,
joined through Cont -- layout/sg13cmos5l-bandgap_top/generate.py's
routing-invariant corollaries). label_layer 8/2 is Metal1.pin, the
curated sg13cmos5l deck's own net-name layer
(EXTRACTION_DECK.metal_labels == ((8, 2),)) and the only layer this
GDS puts net text on: 78 labels including all 8 'vdd' and all 27 'vss'
occurrences (counted on the committed GDS, not assumed).
- vias[]: Cont (6/0) is the single inter-level bridge of this stack,
connecting GatPoly and Metal1. Contacts landing on Activ (source/drain
and emitter/collector taps) share the GDS layer but bridge nothing in
this model -- Activ is not a stackup conductor, it appears only as
active_layer.
- nets[]: vdd and vss, both kind: "supply", which is what makes a short
between them report as the severe erc.supply_short rather than the
general erc.multiply_driven_net. Each must resolve to exactly ONE
electrical island: erc.unconnected_net fires on zero matches and on
more than one (a rail split into pieces that never touch), so ZERO
findings naming either supply is exactly the 'one island per supply'
verdict item 11 requires -- not merely an absence of evidence.
Signal nets (fb, sns1, sns2, vref, ...) are deliberately NOT declared:
item 11 is the structural supply question only.
- ties[]: the n-well tie, declared the way klt's curated sg13cmos5l
deck itself derives tap_nplus (klayout-tools#1273): an n+ well tie is
nSD-covered (7/0) Activ (1/0) inside NWell (31/0), wired up through
Cont to Metal1 (connect_to names the stackup role) and expected to
reach net vdd. tap_layer is the Activ conductor narrowed by
tap_requires: ["7/0"] -- the same boolean-implant shape the gf180mcu
example in klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md uses (Comp ∩ Nplus), because
a bare tap_layer matching every source/drain contact in the well is
the unfalsifiable form the degenerate-tie rule (klayout-tools#2199)
exists to catch. This declaration became gradeable when
klayout-tools#2186 isolated ties[]'s extraction from the primary
connectivity graph: the false erc.supply_short that forced issue
#225 to omit ties[] (klayout-tools#2169) is gone, and gates[]/nets[]
findings are now bit-identical whether ties[] is declared or not.
What the run actually reports on this stream, verified on the
committed GDS (klt 0.5.0+g32f69f811682, 2026-09-22): every physically
distinct NWell island -- 12 of them: the bandgap_core mirror's one
shared well, bandgap_amp's one shared well, and the ten pnpMPA
wells -- carries ZERO nSD-covered Activ, so each is reported under
erc.missing_tie (no tap drawn at all; both failure modes of that
rule). Those findings are kept, not tuned away, per this issue's own
acceptance criteria: the two MOS wells are the already-documented
floating-body gap (layout/README.md 'SG13CMOS5L: LVS -- mismatch,
fully attributed', cause 4 -- no drawn tap means no DC bias path for
the well), and the ten pnpMPA wells are device bodies whose n+ base
ring is drawn marker-less per CMOS5L's own idiom (pSD is the only
implant mask the PDK's PCells draw; n+ is its complement -- see
layout/common_sg13cmos5l.py draw_pnpmpa), which is exactly why the
deck-derived tap expression cannot see them. The findings are filed
as follow-up issue #240 rather than suppressed; item 11's
'zero erc.missing_tie' therefore stays unmet until real taps are
drawn or the marker-less base ring becomes expressible upstream.
The substrate half is deliberately NOT declared and cannot be: this
block sits in native p-substrate with no drawn p-well/tub layer, and
klt erc's ties[] requires drawn well_layer geometry, so a substrate
tie is structurally undeclarable (klayout-tools#2255, still open --
no ties_disclosure can describe the missing half of a stream that
declares its n-well tie either). The substrate-tie evidence that does
stand in for it, counted on the committed GDS: the ten pnpMPA
collector rings are pSD-covered Activ outside every NWell -- the
deck's own tap_pplus shape -- each contacted up to a Metal1 ring
labelled vss (10 polygons, 75.74 um^2 total).
ties_disclosure is omitted on purpose: the tap side IS expressible
(the layers exist and the declaration above is falsifiable), so a
disclosure would downgrade checked work to a considered omission.
erc_coverage.inapplicable's 'no_ties_declared' entry disappears from
the report; the tie work moves to erc_coverage.checked and the
findings above are the verdict of record.
